name: JOKR (Daki)
one_liner: 15-minute grocery delivery from dark stores; after exiting five markets it survives only as Daki in Brazil
story: Ralf Wenzel's JOKR launched in 2021 promising 15-minute grocery delivery from dark stores in New York and Latin America, merged with Brazil's Daki and became a unicorn with a $260M round at a $1.2B valuation in December 2021 (after a R$870M / $170M first round). As funding dried up it pulled out of the US (June 2022), Santiago and Medellin (November 2022) and Mexico (February 2023), then raised about $50M in 2023 at an $800M valuation to focus only on Brazil. Daki kept operating and later reports describe it as breakeven, with iFood taking a minority stake; total_raised counts only the reported rounds.

name: Merqueo
one_liner: Online supermarket delivering groceries from its own dark stores in Colombia, Mexico and Brazil
story: Merqueo built a Bogotá online supermarket with its own warehouses and expanded to Mexico and Brazil while talking up a US IPO. It closed Mexico in June 2022, entered Colombian business reorganisation in May 2023 with about COP 25.2bn (~$5.8M at 2023 rates) of pending obligations, and in July 2025 shut its stores and switched off its app after failing to secure new financing. Total raised is CB Insights' estimate; it also had a reported $22M IDB financing for Brazil.

name: Jüsto
one_liner: Mexico's store-less digital supermarket delivering groceries from its own warehouses
story: Ricardo Weder's Jüsto sold groceries online in Mexico with no physical stores, raising a $152M Series B led by General Atlantic in 2022 that El Financiero billed as minting a new Mexican unicorn, and expanding to Peru. After a $70M equity-plus-debt raise in October 2024 it wound down Peru, then announced it would stop operating in Mexico on 15 December 2025, citing financial, operating and strategic factors and struggling to make the model profitable. Weeks later, in January 2026, OMNi took over the brand and relaunched it, so the original venture ended in a rescue rather than an exit.

name: 123milhas
one_liner: Online travel agency selling cheap tickets built on airline miles and prepaid flexible-date promo trips
story: 123milhas sold discounted air tickets sourced from frequent-flyer miles, then pushed 'Promo123' flexible-date tickets and packages paid upfront for future travel, effectively betting that fares would fall without any hedge. When fares stayed high it suspended the Promo line in August 2023 and on 29 August filed for judicial recovery in Belo Horizonte, declaring R$2.308bn (~$462M at 2023 rates) of debt owed to around 700,000 creditors, most of them customers. Peer Maxmilhas also filed for judicial recovery as the Brazilian online travel sector's prepaid model unravelled.

name: Frubana
one_liner: B2B app supplying fresh produce and groceries to restaurants and small shops in Colombia, Mexico and Brazil
story: Frubana let restaurants and corner shops order produce and groceries wholesale through an app, cutting out middlemen, and expanded from Colombia to Mexico and Brazil. After layoffs in 2022, it announced in February 2024 that it would close Colombia and Mexico to concentrate on Brazil, then shut its last active market there, joining Merqueo among Colombia's high-profile startup closures. Analyses citing CB Insights grouped it with Jüsto as a LatAm example of the post-2022 funding crunch.
